put.summary: Update terms and replace its sections
put.description:
Updates the terms title, version and change summary, then reconciles the sections array: sections missing from the payload are deleted, existing ones updated and new ones created.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check. Destructive replace semantics: any existing section whose id is not present in the sections array is deleted. Section numbers are renumbered in a two-pass update (temp- prefixed) to dodge a unique constraint, so a mid-request failure can leave sections with temp- section numbers.

_Source: `app/api/terms/[id]/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

Deletes all user acceptance records for the terms and then the terms document itself.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check. Permanently deletes the legal acceptance audit trail (userTermsAcceptance rows) for this version. Same query-string-vs-path-param quirk as the duplicate route.

_Source: `app/api/terms/[id]/route.ts`_

_Auth: `none`_

tier.description: Tier number the vendor type may access

ipAddress.description: Client IP recorded for the legal audit trail

userAgent.description: Client user agent recorded for the legal audit trail

acceptanceMethod.description: CHECKBOX, BUTTON_CLICK, SIGNATURE, BIOMETRIC or VOICE. Defaults to CHECKBOX.

deletedBy.description: Who deleted it; defaults to 'admin' in the change log

sections.description: Sections: {sectionNumber, title, content, parentId?, sortOrder=0, isRequired=true, sectionType=CONTENT}. sectionType is one of HEADER, CONTENT, FOOTER, LEGAL_NOTICE, CONTACT_INFO. parentId references another section's sectionNumber.

changesSummary.description: Summary of changes in this version

id.description: Section id - the handler reads this from the BODY, not the path segment

termsId.description: Parent terms id; must exist and be a draft

updatedBy.description: Who made the change; defaults to 'admin' in the change log

changesSummary.description: Summary of what changed in this version

sections.description: Full desired section list. Objects: {id?, title, content, sectionNumber, sortOrder, isRequired, sectionType}. Omitting an existing id DELETES that section.

baseCredits.description: Credit allowance granted at this tier

SuccessMessageEnvelope.description: Envelope `{ success, message }`; `success` is `true` on 2xx and `false` on error responses.

cookieAuth.name: next-auth.session-token
cookieAuth.description: NextAuth JWT session cookie from logging in to the admin panel. On HTTPS the cookie name is `__Secure-next-auth.session-token`.

cronBearer.description: `LINODE_CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token — every cron job goes through `assertCronAuth` in `lib/linode/cron-auth.ts`, which reads only this variable (despite some jobs being non-Linode).

unverifiedAccessToken.name: Authorization
unverifiedAccessToken.description: Legacy customer routes: an `accessToken` cookie or an `Authorization` header must be PRESENT, but the value is never verified. Not real authentication.

adsWebhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
adsWebhookSecret.description: `ADS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, sent either as the `x-webhook-secret` header or as a `secret` field in the JSON body. If the env var is unset the route rejects every call with 401 (it does not fall through to unauthenticated access).

webhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
webhookSecret.description: Generic `x-webhook-secret` header check for an inbound webhook.

cronSecretBearer.description: `CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token, compared with `bearerMatches` in `lib/auth/secret-compare.ts`. Distinct from `cronBearer`, which uses `LINODE_CRON_SECRET`.
